key_insight: Generating plausible protein–ligand binding poses is not the same as identifying the best one. Pyrite introduces a 1,500-pair benchmark where expert chemists using 3D visualization and physics-based scores perform near chance.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how to evaluate systems that rank candidate protein–ligand binding poses—a difficult step between generating molecular structures and selecting useful predictions.
method: Build Pyrite with 1,500 pose pairs spanning diverse protein–ligand complexes.
Frame pose ranking as a pairwise comparison task for evaluating ranking agents.
Measure expert chemist performance with access to 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores.
impact: Pyrite gives AI/ML practitioners a focused benchmark for testing pose-ranking agents. The near-chance expert results highlight the difficulty of the task and caution against assuming that available visual and physics-based signals make ranking straightforward.
visual_elements: Side-by-side 3D views of two ligand poses within the same protein binding pocket.
Pipeline diagram: candidate pose generation → pairwise ranking → selected pose.
Benchmark card highlighting 1,500 pose pairs across diverse complexes.
Qualitative comparison graphic showing expert performance close to a chance baseline, without inventing an exact score.
paper_title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
paper_authors: Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys, Pranav Murugan, Nate Gruver
